subject: Tool-calling integration patterns - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 18:34:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: tool-calling integration patterns + proposed next steps

Hi Samir / Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful session. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- In-chat tool/function calling for account lookup, payments routing, and contract retrieval (PDFs)
- Ability to run parallel tools (lookup + risk-check) and merge structured outputs for the UI
- Deterministic auth model: service account for server-side calls; short-lived tokens for client-initiated flows
- Embeddings + reranker for historical ticket search and suggested responses
- Security/compliance checklist items for SOC2 and retention controls (Alicia flagged)

Suggested integration approach (high-level):
1) SDK + server integration
   - Use Redwood server-side SDK for all tool/function calls that require credentials (payment gateway, contract store).
   - Keep any client-side prompts only for UI composition and streaming; never expose sensitive creds in the browser.
2) Tool definitions + routing
   - Define explicit tool schemas (name, input_schema, output_schema, auth_scope) so the model can emit structured calls.
   - Route by policy: low-latency regional routing for UI-critical flows; fallback to US-central dedicated pool for heavy batch reranking.
3) Parallel tool orchestration
   - Invoke independent lookups (e.g., account lookup + risk-check) in parallel; merge outputs with a small orchestration layer and validate against schemas.
4) Error handling
   - All tool responses should include status codes and error_reason. The model should be prompted with graceful-fallback behaviors on errors (retry, degrade to cached summary, or return safe failure message).
5) Embeddings & reranker
   - Store embeddings in your vector DB; call Redwood embeddings endpoint for upserts/queries and use a lightweight reranker model for top-K precision before presenting to user.

Attachments: I attached a short patterns doc and a sketch of the proposed integration diagram.

Proposed next steps:
- S1: Technical deep dive with Ethan and your platform team to walk SDK auth + tool definitions (45–60m) — suggested window next Tue or Wed.
- S2: Security questionnaire kickoff (Alicia) — we can send the SOC2/controls pack and schedule a 30m sync.
- S3: POC scope: 2-week spike for account lookup + reranker demo (deliverable: working flow + perf numbers).

Can you confirm availability for S1 (Ethan will bring an SDK + routing sample)?

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: tool-calling integration patterns + proposed next steps

Great Qs — answers inline and attaching an SDK snippet.

1) Auth model: we support both patterns. Recommended path for most customers is:
   - Use your STS (short-lived tokens) + Redwood server-side SDK. Client obtains a short-lived session from your backend; backend calls Redwood with a customer-scoped service account token.
   - Redwood can also host a token-exchange endpoint if you'd prefer not to build the STS; we treat that as an add-on integration.

2) Example tool schema (payment_initiate) — attached in the SDK snippets doc, but brief example:
   - name: payment_initiate
   - input_schema: {amount: number, currency: string, account_id: string, idempotency_key: string}
   - output_schema: {status: string, transaction_id: string, error_code?: string, error_message?: string}
   - auth_scope: payments.write

3) Merge conflicts: Redwood's orchestration layer is intentionally lightweight. For record-updates we recommend that the authoritative store implement optimistic concurrency (version or txn id). Pattern: have tools return a 'proposed_change' plus 'base_version'; an external coordinator (your platform) applies the change and returns success/failure to the model. For UI flows where low-latency is required, we provide helper libraries to do a best-effort merge and surface conflict to the user.

Ethan — can you add the SDK code snippet and a short note on routing policies (regional vs fallback) in the doc?

Samir/Alicia — Wed 16–17 EST works; I scheduled a 60m deep dive and included a calendar invite (see related links).

Cheers,
Marissa

Hi all —

Adding a couple of focused notes and a minimal SDK snippet you can drop into your platform:

- Server-side pattern (Node.js pseudo):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY});

async function callPaymentTool(input) {
  return client.callTool('payment_initiate', input, {auth: {type: 'service_account'}});
}

Notes:
- Tool calls with auth: service_account are executed in a server-only context. For user-scoped actions, mint a short-lived token from your STS and pass it as 'user_token' metadata to the SDK call.
- Routing policies: use 'region_preference' header when latency-critical (e.g., UI) flows. Redwood will try regional pool then fallback to dedicated pool you provision.
- Parallel invocation: run client.callTool on Promise.all(...) and then validate outputs against the output_schema before merging. If conflicts, return a structured 'conflict' error to guide the model.

I'll bring a short demo of parallel lookup + reranker in the Wed call.
